title: safe bump and clean legacy optional params across Python/JS/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope:
- Bump a set of non-breaking minor/patch dependencies across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs to address known CVEs and improve TLS/HTTP clients (examples: httpx -> latest minor, cryptography pin updates, undici/undici-compat bump for Node).
- Remove and formally deprecate legacy optional API surface fields that we no longer support on the server side (legacy_auth_header, request_metadata, model_hint). These fields are currently accepted with warnings in the hosted API but complicate SDK surface and tests.
- Regenerate lockfiles, update CI workflows, and add compatibility shims where necessary for a gradual migration.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- All three language SDKs pass full CI (unit + integration) and the runtime test harness against staging.
- No customer-facing errors introduced by dependency upgrades (validated by a staging traffic soak and canary rollout).
- A migration guide published in developer docs explaining removal of legacy fields and recommended replacements.
- Deprecation notices added to SDK release notes and console deprecation banner config.

Plan of work:
1) Inventory: finalize exact package versions for each language and enumerate which transitive deps change. (ENG-728341-INV)
2) Python: bump httpx, cryptography minor, pydantic compatibility pin; regenerate poetry.lock; run integration tests against staging runtime.
3) JS: bump undici/node-fetch or relevant adapter, update ESM/CJS build outputs, regenerate package-lock/yarn.lock, run browser + Node tests.
4) Go: bump HTTP client and protobuf toolchain versions, run go mod tidy/verify, compile with older Go toolchains supported for customers.
5) API surface: add feature flag on server to emit warnings for legacy_auth_header; add SDK switch to continue sending until global rollout completes. Create migration guide and deprecation timeline.
6) Rollout: staged release with canary at 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours, monitor errors, latency, and token cost delta.

Risks / Tradeoffs:
- Some dependency bumps change HTTP behaviour (connection pooling/timeouts) impacting latency. Mitigate via test harness and runtime config overrides.
- Maintaining temporary compatibility shims increases short-term code complexity but reduces customer incidents. We will scope shims to a single release and add automated removal tickets.
- Lockfile churn may cause large PRs; break into per-language PRs for reviewability.

Deliverables:
- Three PRs (python, js, go) with clear CHANGELOG entries and upgrade notes.
- Staging soak and observability dashboard for the canary.
- Developer-facing migration guide on docs.redwood.ai and an internal runbook for SRE.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Safe+Dep+Bumps+and+Deprecation+Plan
- Draft migration guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-migration/legacy-fields
- Runtime dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/XYZ/staging-sdk-canary
- Initial PRs (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls?q=ENG-728341
